newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening higher on follow-through.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening higher on follow-through.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to open higher Monday, boosted by momentum from Thursday's record close, analysts said.
They added that there were no economic data out Monday that could hinder the Dow Jones Industrial Average from climbing closer to the 8,000 mark.
The Dow closed up 100.43 points Thursday at 7895.81, a record, ahead of the three-day Independence Day weekend.

"The absence of economic news, the strong close on Thursday and the steady bond (prices) indicates that we will have a stronger opening," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said Wall Street had been cheered by the Federal Reserve's decision last week to hold interest rates steady.
"I think we'll see a carryover in the exuburance we saw last week," he said, adding that the Dow should go through 8,000 points soon.
Brown said the most attractive sector remained basic industries with large capitalization.
"If the averages are going higher it's those companies that are going to carry them," he said. "That's where the action is."
The key economic data out this week are June producer prices, an indicator of inflation.

The figures are due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT Friday, and economists polled by Reuters expect the overall rate to remain unchanged. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the index is predicted to rise 0.1 percent.
Japan's Nikkei average closed down 262.83 points, or 1.32 percent, at 19,705.17.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 32.4 at 4780.4. Strategists there were betting Wall Street would continue its record run.
The dollar slipped against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 112.20/23 yen. In Europe, the dollar steadied above earlier lows against the mark, trading at 1.7458/68.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was up 4/32 to yield 6.62 percent. The Standard & Poors 500 futures index was up 2.10 to 929.50.

Mario Gabelli, the high-profile fund manager whose firm has nearly $11 billion in assets, has apparently shelved his idea of selling part of his business, The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column.
